summary.headline: Markolines reported FY26 revenue of Rs 348.49 crore (up from Rs 307 crore) and PAT of Rs 26.23 crore (about 15% higher), with EPS up 17% to Rs 11.90.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of Rs 348.49 crore against Rs 307 crore a year earlier, EBITDA of Rs 48.54 crore and PAT of Rs 26.23 crore, with EPS rising from Rs 10.16 to Rs 11.90. Q4 revenue was about Rs 105 crore with a stated PAT margin of about 10.81% and EBITDA margin of about 18%. Management said West Asia-related disruption weighed on performance during the year. The call centred on the pending merger with Markolines Infra, a targeted FY27 growth of at least 30% on a standalone basis, and an active pipeline of about Rs 2,000 crore. Several answers on margins, order book and merger timing were qualitative or repeated.

segments.name: Highway maintenance (pavement)
segments.commentary: About 65% of revenue as of March 2026, per management; Rs 350 crore pavement revenue cited for FY26. Covers preventive, major (5 to 7 year cycle) and rigid pavement maintenance.

segments.name: Specialized construction
segments.commentary: About 35% of revenue as of March 2026, up from about 25% per analyst question; includes micro-surfacing, cold in-place recycling (CIPR), soil stabilisation, FDR, tunnelling and bridges. Management says it carries higher margins.

segments.name: Markolines Infra (proposed merger)
segments.commentary: Cited at about Rs 150 crore FY26 revenue; operates about 60 work orders across about 30 projects including 28 toll projects. Management said its PAT margin is 9 to 10%, above pavement, and monthly billing is about Rs 14 to 15 crore.

segments.name: School and sports infrastructure
segments.commentary: Newly entered; one open school infrastructure order and two smaller sports complex rehabilitation orders in Andhra Pradesh. No value disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of at least 30% on a standalone basis, per management; Markolines Infra revenue would be additional on merger.
Merger with Markolines Infra expected to be completed by end of FY27; management cites about six months for NCLT processes, with all queries answered and none pending.
Target closing order book of at least Rs 1,000 crore by end of FY27.
Target of Rs 1,000 crore revenue scale in about three years, with possibility to bring it forward.
Capex of about Rs 10 crore in FY27 for one or more pavers and possibly one HMP; policy of not exceeding Rs 10 crore per year.
Management expects monsoon at about 90% of average this year; first two quarters to see lower revenue.
capex_capacity: No major capex in FY26, per management.
Plan for one or a few additional pavers and possibly one HMP, about Rs 10 crore in FY27.
Company owns three sets of machinery; other machinery is rented locally where cheaper.
Plants and equipment are churned about every 3 to 4 years to maintain efficiency.
Eligible to bid up to Rs 500 crore projects on its own following completion of a Maharashtra tunnel project.
demand_pricing: Order book about Rs 600 crore plus, split roughly 45-50% maintenance and 50-55% specialized construction (management gave both 50-50 and 45-45 figures). Infra order book is separate and recurring.
Active pipeline of about Rs 2,000 crore across four to five projects of Rs 300 to 500 crore each; management says it wins at least 50% of targeted orders.
L1 position on a Rs 120 crore maintenance contract with a corporation, per management.
Management says it works on a cost-plus basis with clients, so PBT and PAT margins are steady (7 to 8%), while EBITDA varies with client capex pass-through.
Management says maintenance is about 15% of road cost in India versus about 40% globally, which it sees as a long-term driver.
Government allowed sovereign and international funds to participate in PPP highway construction, which management sees as increasing demand for O&M partners.

qa_highlights.question: Status of merger with Markolines Infra and expected completion?
qa_highlights.answer: Applications filed and all queries answered in March, with few recently answered; management expects about six months to completion and a merged entity by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA margins of Infra and combined FY27 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Infra results to be released within a week after final audit; Infra margins are higher than pavement, with PAT of about 9 to 10% for services. Management later said PBT and PAT margins stay at 7 to 8%.

qa_highlights.question: FY26 and FY27 capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: No major capex in FY26; about Rs 10 crore planned in FY27 for pavers and possibly one HMP, with equipment churned every 3 to 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Win ratio and closing order book expectations for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Win ratio of at least 50% on targeted active orders; management targets a closing order book of at least Rs 1,000 crore, versus an 18-month typical coverage norm.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth of at least 30% standalone, driven by higher eligibility after the tunnel project; margin guidance was not given, as EBITDA is said to vary with client capex pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall in Q4, and what drove the 62% QoQ PAT jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other expenses and material consumption must be viewed together because outsourcing shifts costs between heads, and margins should be similar. Q4 is seasonally strongest as billing concentrates in March.

risks_watch: Merger timing relies on NCLT approval; management expects completion within about six months.
Q4 seasonality: first two quarters are weaker due to monsoon, and management expects below-average rainfall this year.
Order book conversion: management's 50% win-rate claim and Rs 1,000 crore closing order book target are unverified.
Specialized construction share rising (about 35%), with the 50% of order book in multi-year contracts, which affects visibility and execution timing.
Margin variability: EBITDA is described as variable with client capex pass-through; PAT margin guidance is only 7 to 8%.
West Asia crisis cited as a drag on FY26 performance; no detail given on impact.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term structural demand, merger benefits and growth targets. Evasive on specifics: EBITDA, margin, capex and order-book breakdowns were given loosely or repeated, and several questions were deflected to earlier answers.

we are expecting a very good growth this year to the tune of at least 30%.
We are expecting that we should have an at least 1000 crore order book.
